== con-leche/ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean#L90-L117
    90  /-- **The main theorem.**  Every environment the checker accepts has a
    91  model in every set theory — at every `Nat.div`/`Nat.mod` pin list, so
    92  consistency does not depend on which variants the install gate is
    93  handed (the empty list included: under it every stream that declares
    94  `Nat.div` declines).  The shipped binary runs the fold at
    95  `natOpPinSets`. -/
    96  theorem model_exists (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
    97      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (ds : Array Declaration) (env : Env)
    98      (accepted : checkDecls .verified pins ds = .ok env) :
    99      Nonempty (Model V env) := by
   100    obtain ⟨m⟩ := Cached.checkDecls_sound (V := V) rfl accepted
   101    exact ⟨Model.Model.ofEnvModelM m⟩
   102  
   103  open Frontend in
   104  /-- **The main corollary.**  A file declaring a theorem of type `False`
   105  in the shape `jsonWithTheoremFalse` describes is rejected: the parse
   106  reads the template's four lines into a theorem record of type `False`,
   107  the preparation keeps the record, and a stream holding it is never
   108  accepted.  At every pin list, as the main theorem: the shipped binary
   109  runs the fold at `natOpPinSets`. -/
   110  theorem no_False_declaration (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
   111      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (chunks : List ByteArray)
   112      (h : jsonWithTheoremFalse chunks) :
   113      ∃ e, (do
   114        let pre ← builtinPreludeE
   115        let r ← parseChunks chunks
   116        let ds := preparePrelude pre r.decls
   117        checkDecls .verified pins ds) = .error e := by

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L87-L210
    87  const USAGE: &str = "\
    88  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>] [--no-mark-persistent]
    89                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
    90                 FILE.ndjson
    91         con-ron --help
    92  
    93    (C), the Rust arena checker of con-ron's DESIGN.md section 8: con-leche's
    94    pure checker over an append-only DAG of per-constructor handle arrays, with
    95    con-leche's command line and con-leche's exit codes, so that
    96    scripts/diff-e2e.sh can run the same 383 fixtures against this binary and
    97    the Lean twin `con-ron-lean` alike.  A term is a u32 handle into a Vec: on
    98    the checking path there is no Arc, no tagged pointer and no reference count
    99    at all.  (The PINNED DATA the checker compares against is still
   100    con-leche's own constants as Expr values, interned into the persistent tier
   101    once at startup -- crates/con-ron-core/src/lib.rs says why.)
   102  
   103    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   104                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   105                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists), so a stream
   106                      declaring a theorem of type False is never accepted.  The
   107                      same two statements are PROVED about this program's
   108                      pipeline (ConRon.Capstone.model_exists and
   109                      no_False_declaration, on the Aeneas model of the Rust),
   110                      using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and
   111                      Quot.sound.  What they still assume are hypotheses, not
   112                      axioms: that the driver runs the extracted stages in the
   113                      order it does on the file's bytes, that the unextracted
   114                      Rust in-process modeller answers as the Lean twin's does,
   115                      that the pins are the embedded text, and that the
   116                      committed prelude bytes are con-leche's (a gate, not a
   117                      proof).  OVERVIEW.md section 3.1 lists them.
   118    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   119                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   120                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   121    --jobs=<n>        the check phase runs on <n> worker threads sharing the
   122                      persistent tier and the installed index by reference
   123                      (DESIGN.md section 8.3): each worker owns a scratch tier,
   124                      its own caches and a copy of the pin handles, and the
   125                      results are merged by record index and walked in record
   126                      order, so the verdict and the record a rejection names are
   127                      the same at every <n>.  Default: one per hardware thread,
   128                      capped at 16.  A worker reserves 1 GiB of stack, which a
   129                      `ulimit -v` must allow for.  0 or a non-numeral is a usage
   130                      error, as in con-leche.
   131    --no-mark-persistent
   132                      ACCEPTED AND A NO-OP, for a stronger reason than the
   133                      `con-ron` binary's: the mark it turns off is a
   134                      Lean-runtime reference-counting device
   135                      (Runtime.markPersistent), and this checker has no
   136                      reference counts at all -- a term is a u32 handle into a
   137                      Vec and the persistent tier is immutable in phase B.  A
   138                      run that passes it says so on stderr.
   139    --progress[=<stride>]
   140                      opt-in progress heartbeat on STDERR, one line shape per
   141                      phase:
   142                        con-ron: parse done: <N> fold records ... t=<s>s
   143                        con-ron: install <i>/<N> <decl> t=<s>s
   144                        con-ron: install done: <N>/<N> ..., <M> pending
   145                        con-ron: check <done>/<M> <kind> <name> t=<s>s
   146                        con-ron: check done: <M>/<M> t=<s>s
   147                        con-ron: done: parse <p>s, install <i>s, check <c>s
   148                      An install line is printed BEFORE every <stride>-th
   149                      declaration is installed, so a run that dies in the
   150                      install phase names the declaration it died in on its last
   151                      line; a check line is printed AFTER every <stride>-th
   152                      COMPLETED check.  On a failure the phase's closing line
   153                      says so and the summary still prints.  Bare --progress is
   154                      stride 1; a stride that is not a decimal numeral, or 0, is
   155                      a usage error.
   156    --pins FILE       con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: read the pin list from a
   157                      `con-ron-pins/1` dump instead of the core's own embedded
   158                      text (task #43), through the UNVERIFIED reader.  The pins
   159                      are interned into the persistent tier at startup, before
   160                      the fold (DESIGN.md section 8.6 P2d).
   161    --no-pins         con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: the empty pin list, the pin
   162                      loop's `[]` arm, under which a Nat.div/Nat.mod stream
   163                      declines.  Neither flag is needed for a normal run: the
   164                      pins are con-leche's `natOpPinSets`, embedded in the
   165                      verified core and decoded by it.
   166    --help            print this text on STDOUT and exit 0, in any argument
   167                      position; no input is read.  Its last line names the
   168                      global allocator THIS binary was built with (below), so a
   169                      measurement can be reproduced.
   170  
   171  build-time selection (cargo features, not command-line flags): the global
   172  allocator is `con-ron-dump`'s `#[global_allocator]`, chosen on this crate's
   173  dependency edge -- `cargo build --release` is mimalloc, `--no-default-features`
   174  is glibc `malloc`, and `--no-default-features --features jemalloc` is jemalloc.
   175  It is the same edge `crates/con-ron` has, so the two checkers are measured on
   176  the same allocator unless a build says otherwise.
   177  
   178  Any other option is a usage error: the run reports it, prints this text and
   179  exits 3 without reading its input.
   180  
   181  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.
   182  An out-of-memory condition is NEITHER: this program aborts the way Rust aborts
   183  on a failed allocation ('memory allocation of <n> bytes failed', SIGABRT,
   184  which a shell reports as 134).  A panic is exit 3.
   185  
   186  THE VERDICT LINE'S COUNT.  It counts the FILE's accepted declaration RECORDS:
   187  one per def/theorem/opaque/axiom/inductive/quot record the file declares.  The
   188  built-in prelude's own records are not counted, and neither are the records
   189  the in-process modeller generates; a stream record that declares a prelude
   190  declaration IS counted.  That count is a property of the INPUT; the number of
   191  environment CONSTANTS is not.
   192  
   193  THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE.  Every run installs, first and unconditionally, the
   194  checker's own little prelude -- the six pinned basis blocks (Eq, Nat, PUnit,
   195  Empty, False, Quot) and the toolchain's Bool and And blocks, embedded at build
   196  time -- so the pin-certified Nat operations find their ground whatever order
   197  the export chose.  It is parsed into the SAME store as the stream, which is
   198  what the persistent tier is for: the prelude's nodes and the stream's are
   199  hash-consed together.
   200  
   201  environment (con-leche's):
   202    CON_LECHE_INMODEL=0          turn the in-process modeller off; a mutual or
   203                                 nested block is then pushed bare and the FOLD
   204                                 declines it, having found no route
   205    CON_LECHE_INMODEL_CENSUS=1   report every mutual/nested block's outcome
   206                                 after the parse and stop (exit 2)
   207    CON_LECHE_PROJREC_TRACE      name each rewritten projection function
   208  These are the in-process modeller's debug switches and they go with it: no
   209  environment variable this program reads can shape a verdict, which is
   210  con-leche's own rule -- every such switch is a command-line flag.";

    18  //! | exit | verdict | meaning |
    19  //! |---|---|---|
    20  //! | 0 | `accepted N declarations` | every declaration checked; `N` counts the file's declaration records |
    21  //! | 1 | `rejected` | a declaration is invalid |
    22  //! | 2 | `declined` | the checker positively detected a feature it does not support, and says which |
    23  //! | 3 | error | bad usage, malformed input, or an internal failure of unclear cause |

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L14-L119
    14  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    15  
    16  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    17  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    18  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    19  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's two headline theorems in the shape
    20  the original campaign used (`conron.model_exists` /
    21  `conron.no_False_declaration`, `proof/ConRon/RefineOld/Main.lean`):
    22  
    23  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — every environment the Aeneas model of the
    24    Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    25  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    26    type `False` is never accepted by it.
    27  
    28  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    29  frontier is measured as the dependency closure of these two, and it is
    30  EMPTY since `arena` `db1131f1` (task #97-MILESTONE): both depend on
    31  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` only (§4's census).  What they
    32  still assume is exactly their hypotheses, listed below.
    33  
    34  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    35  
    36  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    37  around six extracted core functions, in this order, on one `AState` made
    38  from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    39  
    40      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    41        → prepare_prelude → intern_all_pins → (the declaration fold)
    42  
    43  and the twin's `Arena.runPipeline` (`Arena/Main.lean`) is the same six
    44  stages with `installThenCheck` last.  **The sixth stage is the fold the
    45  binary's driver runs, pool and all** (task #97-P5-POOL):
    46  `driver::check_decls_driver` runs phase A with the heartbeat as its hook,
    47  freezes the tier, runs phase B on `pool::check_pool`, and thaws the tier.
    48  The stage hypothesis is `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`: phase
    49  A accepted, the freeze accepted, and one accepting `check_pending_worker`
    50  per worker over the records that worker checked, together covering the
    51  pending records — every call a verified one.  That the pool's accept has
    52  this shape is the pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of
    53  `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.  The sequential walk
    54  `check_decls_phased` is one such pool (`poolAccepts_of_check_decls_phased`).
    55  The theorems hold for EVERY install hook, so they cover the plain run and
    56  `--progress` alike.  `pool_accepts_refines` relates the stage to the twin's
    57  `Arena.PooledAccepts`, and `Bridge/Checker/Phased.lean`'s
    58  `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` carries that to the pure fold.  So the
    59  statement takes the six Rust RUNS as hypotheses (the driver's calling order
    60  is the one trusted line, exactly as it was for the original campaign), and
    61  the proof is:
    62  
    63  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s six `…_refines` lemmas walk the
    64     Rust runs into six TWIN runs from the twin's own start state
    65     `AState.init EStore.empty`, related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/
    66     `AStateInv`: lockstep);
    67  2. **Theorem 1** — the twin runs feed `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge`, whose
    68     pure fold accepts the denoted stream: con-leche's
    69     `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` gives the model, and
    70     `no_False_theorem_accepted_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream
    71     (`stages_no_False`, `Arena.no_False_declaration_pipeline`'s route through
    72     the pure fold);
    73  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a
    74     model.
    75  
    76  Every step is an existing theorem; what this file adds is glue: the Rust
    77  runs threaded through `Sim₀`/`SimStream`/`SimFold`, and the one twin-store
    78  fact the composition needs from Theorem 1 — `StoreWF` at the headline's
    79  `AStateRel` (`stages_storeWF`) — read off its stage lemmas.  Theorem 2 itself
    80  carries no fact about the twin's store (task #97-T2-AUDIT).
    81  
    82  ## The named hypotheses
    83  
    84  The tiers have no `sorry` left on the roots' closure, so these hypotheses
    85  (beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the run facts `hpers`/`hest`/`hst0`/
    86  `h1`…`h6` and `hfalse`) are the whole of what the two theorems assume.
    87  Struck-through entries were hypotheses once and are theorems now (DESIGN.md's
    88  task #97-COMPOSE section tags each with its owning lane):
    89  
    90  * ~~`InitRel`~~ — the Rust start state is related to the twin's: a theorem
    91    since task #97-P5-Top (`Refine2/Checker/Init.lean`'s `init_rel`);
    92  * ~~`hk : CoreSpec .verified Arena.checkFuel`~~ — Theorem 1's Core tier
    93    spec: a theorem since task #97-P3-Core round 6
    94    (`Bridge/Checker/Hyp.lean`'s `CoreSpec.of_core`, passed here);
    95  * ~~`hind : IndSpec .verified`~~ — Theorem 1's inductive tier spec:
    96    discharged by `Bridge/Inductives/Decl.lean`'s `indSpec_of_bridge` since task
    97    #97-P3-Ind round 8 (the two headline theorems build it; the stage lemmas
    98    below still take it as a parameter);
    99  * `hbytes` — the prelude gate (`scripts/gen-prelude-lean.sh --check`);
   100  * ~~`hsc : ScanSpec`~~ — Theorem 2's scanner seam: a theorem since task
   101    #97-P5-Front (`Refine2/Frontend/Scan/Spec.lean`'s `scanSpec`);
   102  * `hmr : Refine2.Frontend.ModellerRefines inst m inProcessModeller` — the
   103    Rust modeller against the twin's (the modeller seam, by design): the
   104    unextracted `crates/con-ron/src/in_model/`, a port of con-leche's
   105    `InModel.generate`, answers what the twin's `inProcessModeller` (which
   106    CALLS con-leche's `generate`) answers;
   107  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks
   108    (task #97-P5-Driver): the binary parses with the verified reader loop
   109    `parse_source` over the driver's file handle, and
   110    `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that
   111    `parse_chunks` over the chunks the handle hands out; that the handle hands
   112    out the file's bytes, in order, is the input seam, as `hmr` is the
   113    modeller's;
   114  * `hdec : kernel.pins_decode.decode text = ok (.Ok pins)` — the pin list is
   115    what the port's decoder read (it was `hwf`, the list's well-formedness,
   116    until task #97-P5-Top ported `RefineOld/PinsWF.lean`'s `decode_wf` to
   117    `Refine2/Checker/PinsWF.lean`); the binary's `pins_for_run` choosing the
   118    text is driver code.
   119  -/

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L530-L560
   530  theorem no_False_declaration (V : Type w) [ConLeche.SetTheory V]
   531      (hbytes : ConRon.Arena.Frontend.preludeText =
   532        ConLeche.Frontend.builtinPreludeText.toUTF8)
   533      {G : Type} {inst : frontend.types.Modeller G} {m : G}
   534      (hmr : ConRon.Refine2.Frontend.ModellerRefines inst m
   535        ConRon.Arena.Frontend.inProcessModeller)

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L15
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle:
     5  //!
     6  //! ```text
     7  //! bits 31…28   ctor tag   (4 bits, high)
     8  //! bit  27      tier       (0 = persistent, 1 = scratch)
     9  //! bits 26…0    index      into THAT CONSTRUCTOR'S array of THAT TIER
    10  //! ```
    11  //!
    12  //! so 134 217 728 nodes per constructor per tier, and — the point of putting
    13  //! the tier *above* the index rather than in the low bit (con-leche's lesson
    14  //! 6) — a persistent handle's bits never change when the scratch tier comes
    15  //! and goes.

   165  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Handle.lean:73-83 BMIdx` — `BMIdx`, a handle
   166  /// into the **binder datum store**: the same word layout as the other four (tag
   167  /// 0, the tier bit, the index), for a store with ONE constructor and so no tag
   168  /// to spend.
   169  ///
   170  /// DESIGN.md §8.3 gives `lam`/`forallE` a `BinderMeta` INSIDE the node
   171  /// record, which makes the record twenty-four bytes with a `PropWhen` — and
   172  /// a `PropWhen` is `Arc`-carrying at `one`/`two`/`many`, so every `dup2` of a
   173  /// binder record is a reference count and every cons probe of the binder
   174  /// tables compares one (task #97-P6-10 §3 priced the pair at 2–3 % of
   175  /// `Init`).  With the datum interned the record is three `u32`s of POD, its
   176  /// hash is `pack2`-shaped like the other nine, and its `eq2` is three word
   177  /// comparisons.
   178  pub struct BMIdx {
   179      pub word: u32,
   180  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L4160-L4195
  4160      /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:501-521 EStore.intern
  4161      /// Hash-cons an expression node: probe the persistent cons table, then the
  4162      /// scratch one, then append to the tier the store is in (DESIGN.md §8.3).
  4163      /// The cap test is the Lean's `capOK` turned into the `Native` decline
  4164      /// §8.3 puts here.
  4165      ///
  4166      /// **Dispatched ONCE** (task #97-P6-15).  The body below used to run the
  4167      /// whole sequence over the `ENodeView`, and each of its four steps
  4168      /// dispatched on the view's tag again and built the node record again:
  4169      /// the persistent probe built it (inside `ETables::find`), the scratch
  4170      /// probe built it a second time, `der_of_view` re-dispatched to compute
  4171      /// the derived word, and `ETables::push` re-dispatched and built it a
  4172      /// third time to append it.  A binder paid `binder_meta_dup` at each of
  4173      /// the three.  So the tag is read once here and the ten per-constructor
  4174      /// paths below each build their record ONCE and hand the same `&r` to the
  4175      /// two probes, to the capacity test and to the push — the same clauses in
  4176      /// the same order, with the dispatch and the two rebuilds gone.
  4177      ///
  4178      /// The twin's `intern` is one `def` over `ENodeView`; what is owed is the
  4179      /// ten-arm spelling and `internC v = intern (view of C)` per constructor,
  4180      /// each of them `rfl` after the `match`.
  4181      pub fn intern(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, v: ENodeView) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  4182          match v {
  4183              ENodeView::BVar(i) => self.intern_bvar(pers, i),
  4184              ENodeView::FVar(idx, ty) => self.intern_fvar(pers, idx, ty),
  4185              ENodeView::Sort(u) => self.intern_sort(pers, u),
  4186              ENodeView::Const(n, us) => self.intern_const(pers, n, us),
  4187              ENodeView::App(f, a) => self.intern_app(pers, f, a),
  4188              ENodeView::Lam(ty, body, m) => self.intern_lam(pers, ty, body, m),
  4189              ENodeView::ForallE(ty, body, m) => self.intern_forall_e(pers, ty, body, m),
  4190              ENodeView::LetE(ty, val, body) => self.intern_let_e(pers, ty, val, body),
  4191              ENodeView::Lit(l) => self.intern_lit(pers, l),
  4192              ENodeView::Proj(n, i, e) => self.intern_proj(pers, n, i, e),
  4193          }
  4194      }
  4195  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L4453-L4501
  4453      pub fn intern_app(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, f: EIdx, a: EIdx) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  4454          let r: AppNode = AppNode { f, a };
  4455          let sk: bool = if self.scratch_on {
  4456              if r.f.is_persistent() {
  4457                  !r.a.is_persistent()
  4458              } else {
  4459                  true
  4460              }
  4461          } else {
  4462              false
  4463          };
  4464          let hit: Option<EIdx> = if sk {
  4465              None
  4466          } else if self.shared_on {
  4467              pers.e.apps.find(&r)
  4468          } else {
  4469              self.pers.apps.find(&r)
  4470          };
  4471          match hit {
  4472              Some(hp) => Ok(hp),
  4473              None => {
  4474                  if self.scratch_on {
  4475                      let at: (usize, Option<EIdx>) = self.scr.apps.find_slot(&r);
  4476                      match at.1 {
  4477                          Some(hs) => Ok(hs),
  4478                          None => {
  4479                              if self.scr.apps.full() {
  4480                                  Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  4481                              } else {
  4482                                  let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  4483                                  let h: EIdx =
  4484                                      EIdx::pack(ETAG_APP, TIER_S, self.scr.apps.size() as u32);
  4485                                  self.scr.apps.push_at(at.0, r, d, h.dup2());
  4486                                  Ok(h)
  4487                              }
  4488                          }
  4489                      }
  4490                  } else if self.shared_on {
  4491                      Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_FROZEN)))
  4492                  } else if self.pers.apps.full() {
  4493                      Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  4494                  } else {
  4495                      let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  4496                      let h: EIdx = EIdx::pack(ETAG_APP, TIER_P, self.pers.apps.size() as u32);
  4497                      self.pers.apps.push(r, d, h.dup2());
  4498                      Ok(h)
  4499                  }
  4500              }
  4501          }

 11708  pub fn flush_caches(st: &mut AState) {
 11709      st.caches.reset();
 11710  }
 11711  
 11712  /// con-leche: none — **the per-declaration bracket, closed** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 11713  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3895-3903 dropScratch` — drop the
 11714  /// scratch tier of the store and the cache entries that name it, in one
 11715  /// operation, so the two halves cannot drift apart.
 11716  pub fn drop_scratch(st: &mut AState) {
 11717      flush_caches(st);
 11718      st.store.drop_scratch();
 11719  }
 11720  
 11721  /// con-leche: none — **the per-declaration bracket, opened** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 11722  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:3905-3912 enterScratch` — turn the
 11723  /// scratch tier on, and clear the per-call memo tables of `Memos`, which
 11724  /// belong to no tier and whose keys the new tier may reuse.
 11725  pub fn enter_scratch(st: &mut AState) {
 11726      st.memos.reset();
 11727      st.store.enable_scratch();

     1  //! `arena::promote` — the scratch → persistent copy (DESIGN.md §8.3, task #97-P6-2).
     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Promote.lean`, declaration for
     4  //! declaration, under DESIGN.md §8.6's lockstep ruling.
     5  //!
     6  //! DESIGN.md §8.3, "**Phase A runs in the scratch tier too, with promotion**":
     7  //!
     8  //! > The install phase (annotate the type and the value, infer, defeq) was
     9  //! > interning every intermediate into the persistent tier — on `Init` 5.06 M
    10  //! > permanent nodes on top of the parse's 6.14 M (+82 %) […].  The arena's
    11  //! > answer is con-leche #64's: phase A opens the scratch tier like phase B,
    12  //! > and the two handles it must keep (the annotated type, the annotated
    13  //! > value) are **promoted** — a memoised structural copy scratch →
    14  //! > persistent […] before the tier is dropped.  Persistent handles are
    15  //! > promoted to themselves.
    16  //!
    17  //! This module is that copy, at all four handle kinds and lifted to
    18  //! `arena::env`'s declaration layer, plus `promote_new` — the entry
    19  //! `arena::checker`'s two fold steps call, which promotes a step's NEWLY
    20  //! INSTALLED constants in place.
    21  //!
    22  //! ## What it is
    23  //!
    24  //! `view` the node, promote its children, `intern` the result into the
    25  //! PERSISTENT tier (`arena::store`'s `intern_persistent` family, whose section
    26  //! note carries the WF obligations).  Three properties make it cheap and make
    27  //! it right:
    28  //!
    29  //! * **a persistent handle promotes to itself**, by one tier-bit test
    30  //!   (`is_persistent`) and no store access at all.  Most of an annotated term
    31  //!   IS the parsed term — `annotate` rebuilds only the spine it changes — so
    32  //!   the walk stops at the first persistent node on every branch;
    33  //! * **the memo makes it `O(result)`** and not `O(unfolding)`: the subject is
    34  //!   a hash-consed DAG, and an unmemoised structural copy of a DAG is the
    35  //!   mistake task #97g's item 5 found three times over.  The memo is per
    36  //!   DECLARATION — a scratch handle means nothing once the tier is dropped —
    37  //!   and it is threaded as an argument-and-result pair, a moved
    38  //!   `ron::HashMap` returned, which is `frontend::proj_rec`'s spelling for its
    39  //!   `seen` set and `arena::expr_ops`' for the three memoized scope walks;
    40  //! * **`intern_persistent` probes the persistent cons table first**, so

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L1394-L1415
  1394  pub fn freeze_tier(ar: &mut EStore) -> Result<PersTier, CheckError> {
  1395      if ar.shared_on || ar.lss.shared_on || ar.lss.ls.shared_on || ar.lss.ls.ns.shared_on {
  1396          Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_REFREEZE)))
  1397      } else {
  1398          let n: NTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.ns.pers, NTables::empty());
  1399          let l: LTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.pers, LTables::empty());
  1400          let ls: LsTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.pers, LsTables::empty());
  1401          let e: ETables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.pers, ETables::empty());
  1402          ar.shared_on = true;
  1403          ar.lss.shared_on = true;
  1404          ar.lss.ls.shared_on = true;
  1405          ar.lss.ls.ns.shared_on = true;
  1406          Ok(PersTier { n, l, ls, e })
  1407      }
  1408  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L1340-L1369
  1340  
  1341  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:384-392 EStore
  1342  /// **The persistent tier of all four stores, as one value `n` phase-B workers
  1343  /// read by reference** — DESIGN.md §8.3's "the persistent tier is immutable in
  1344  /// phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — no atomics anywhere", made
  1345  /// expressible.
  1346  ///
  1347  /// Each store keeps its own `pers` field, which is the tier the PARSE and
  1348  /// phase A append to, and a `shared_on` flag beside `scratch_on`.  While the
  1349  /// flag is off — the parse, phase A, every test, and the whole single-lane
  1350  /// run — each persistent read goes to the owned field and the computation is
  1351  /// the one the tip performed, node for node.  While it is on, the owned field
  1352  /// is empty, a persistent append is refused (`M_FROZEN`) and every persistent
  1353  /// read goes to this record, which the driver holds and every worker borrows.
  1354  ///
  1355  /// **Why a shared PARAMETER and not a field of the state.**  Task #97-P6-6
  1356  /// measured a region inside the threaded `&mut` state eight ways: a bare
  1357  /// `&u64` field on `AState` costs five function bodies Aeneas cannot
  1358  /// translate and the same borrow inside the four stores costs sixteen, while
  1359  /// everything else this split needs — the two-tier layout, the flag, the
  1360  /// value-returning readers below — extracts at zero errors.  So the sharing
  1361  /// arrives as an ordinary shared parameter, the shape `fe: &IFEnv` and `mode:
  1362  /// &CheckMode` already have, and the twin's monad becomes `ReaderT PersTier
  1363  /// (StateT AState (Except CheckError))`.
  1364  pub struct PersTier {
  1365      pub n: NTables,
  1366      pub l: LTables,
  1367      pub ls: LsTables,
  1368      pub e: ETables,
  1369  }

   142  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-P6-6b); the frozen-tier guard
   143  /// `"arena: append to a frozen persistent tier"`, as code points — **the
   144  /// frozen-tier guard**.  A store whose persistent tier is SHARED
   145  /// (`shared_on`) may append to its scratch tier and to nothing else: a
   146  /// persistent append would hand back a handle whose index names a node of the
   147  /// shared tier, which is the one way the split could lose `denoteE`'s
   148  /// injectivity.  Phase B never takes the branch — `check_pending` opens the
   149  /// scratch tier before any term is built, and `intern_persistent`'s only
   150  /// caller is `arena::promote`, which is phase A's — so the guard states the
   151  /// discipline rather than walking a path the run takes.  It is raised as the
   152  /// port's own `Native` decline (task #97-P5-Usize, the maintainer's ruling):

   154  /// nothing when it fires, exactly as for the capacity guard beside it.

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/hashmap2.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; a second `Std.HashMap` replacement, proved
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::HashMap2<K, V>` — proved in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean`
     4  //! (task #97-HM2; designed in task #97-P6-4b).  The same abstract object as
     5  //! `ron::hashmap`'s `HashMap` — a partial map from `K` to `V`, with
     6  //! `Hashable`/`Eq2`/`Dup` as its dictionaries and the same eleven operations
     7  //! — over an **open-addressed, epoch-stamped, flat slot vector** instead of
     8  //! the Aeneas tutorial's chained buckets.  `ron::hashmap` is untouched and
     9  //! keeps its proofs (`proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap.lean`); this module's are
    10  //! in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean` (task #97-HM2).
    11  //!
    12  //! **Why it exists.**  Task #97-P6-1 left `clear_slots + allocate_slots +
    13  //! move_elements*` at 21.8 % of `Init`, "all halving recursions over chained
    14  //! buckets".  Task #97-P6-4b counted what those recursions actually do on
    15  //! `Init`, and the counts name the representation rather than the code:
    16  //!
    17  //! | on `Init`, `ron::HashMap` | count |
    18  //! |---|---:|
    19  //! | `get` calls | 1 228 953 968 |
    20  //! | — resolved in 0 or 1 chain step | 98.8 % |
    21  //! | `insert` calls | 627 320 951 |
    22  //! | **`clear` calls** | **36 053 620** |
    23  //! | **— buckets walked by them** | **2 940 488 064** |
    24  //! | — entries those buckets held | 586 917 896 |
    25  //! | buckets pushed by `allocate_slots` | 948 184 512 |
    26  //! | entries moved by `move_elements*` | 349 323 629 |
    27  //!
    28  //! So the chains are *already* short — the table is a good hash table — and
    29  //! essentially all of the 21.8 % is the per-bucket cost of **emptying and
    30  //! re-growing** the slot vector: 2.94 G bucket writes to clear 0.59 G entries
    31  //! (five buckets walked per entry cleared; the average cleared table is 82
    32  //! buckets holding 16 entries) and 0.95 G `Vec::push`es to allocate them back.
    33  //! Nothing a better chain walk can do touches that.
    34  //!
    35  //! **The representation.**
    36  //!
    37  //! * `slots : Vec<Slot<K, V>>`, `Slot` = `Vacant | Live(u32, K, V)`.  No
    38  //!   `Box`, no chain, no allocation per entry — an entry *is* a slot.
    39  //! * A `Live` slot is **live only if its stamp is the table's `epoch`**;
    40  //!   a `Live` slot with a stale stamp is free space, indistinguishable from

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L356-L580
   356  fn check_main(a: &Args, file: &str) -> u8 {
   357      let t0 = Instant::now();
   358      let mode_tag = if a.verified {
   359          "--verified"
   360      } else {
   361          "--trusted"
   362      };
   363      let mode = if a.verified {
   364          CheckMode::Verified
   365      } else {
   366          CheckMode::Trusted
   367      };
   368      // ONE store for the whole run: the prelude, the stream and the pins are
   369      // hash-consed together into its persistent tier (DESIGN.md §8.3).
   370      let mut st = AState::init(EStore::empty());
   371      // THE PERSISTENT TIER a phase-B worker reads (DESIGN.md §8.3, task
   372      // #97-P6-6b).  The parse and phase A own their own — `shared_on` is
   373      // false on every store until the boundary — so what they are handed here
   374      // is the EMPTY tier, and the single-lane computation is unchanged.  Phase
   375      // B freezes the store's tier into a `PersTier` and hands `&` it to every
   376      // worker; `check_decls_driver` is where that happens.
   377      let pers: &PersTier = &PersTier::empty();
   378      // THE RESERVED-NAME PINS, interned once into that persistent tier before
   379      // anything else touches it (task #97-P6-4a, `arena::pins`): the scratch
   380      // tier is closed here, so every pinned handle is persistent and survives
   381      // every `drop_scratch` of the run.  Until this has run, every `pin_*`
   382      // read raises `Internal` rather than answering — which is what makes the
   383      // initialisation-order hazard task #97c named impossible rather than
   384      // unlikely.
   385      match con_ron_core::arena::pins::intern_reserved_pins(pers, &mut st) {
   386          Ok(()) => (),
   387          Err(e) => {
   388              eprintln!(
   389                  "con-ron: the reserved-name pins do not intern ({}) ({})",
   390                  con_ron::driver::message(&e),
   391                  mode_tag
   392              );
   393              return 3;
   394          }
   395      }
   396      // The in-process modeller, which the parse takes as a type parameter: the
   397      // arena core is quantified over an arbitrary `Modeller`, and this is the
   398      // one the binary supplies — `crates/con-ron`'s own generator behind a
   399      // readback (`con_ron::in_model`).
   400      let modeller = InProcess::new();
   401      // THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE, parsed into that store before anything else.
   402      let prelude_ix = match prelude::builtin_prelude_e(pers, &modeller, &mut st) {
   403          Ok(p) => p,
   404          Err((e, line)) => {
   405              let what = match classify(&e) {
   406                  FrontendClass::Internal(m) => format!("does not parse (line {}: {})", line, m),
   407                  FrontendClass::Declined(w) => format!("is unsupported ({})", w),
   408                  FrontendClass::Invalid(w) => format!("contradicts itself ({})", w),
   409              };
   410              eprintln!(
   411                  "con-ron: the built-in prelude {}; regenerate it with \
   412                   `lake exe natop-pins-export` ({})",
   413                  what, mode_tag
   414              );
   415              return 3;
   416          }
   417      };
   418      let in_model = !env_is("CON_LECHE_INMODEL", "0");
   419      let census = env_is("CON_LECHE_INMODEL_CENSUS", "1");
   420      // Streaming frontend: the file is read 4 MiB at a time and each buffer is
   421      // parsed and dropped, so neither a wholesale text buffer nor a scratch
   422      // file exists.  What comes out is the FILE's records as HANDLES into the
   423      // store above (plus the in-process modeller's).
   424      let parsed: ParseResultD = match driver::parse_export_stream_d(
   425          pers,
   426          &modeller,
   427          &mut st,
   428          file,
   429          in_model,
   430          census,
   431          export_c::CHUNK_SIZE,
   432      ) {
   433          Err(e) => {
   434              eprintln!("con-ron: {}: {}", file, e);
   435              return 3;
   436          }
   437          Ok((Err((e, line)), _)) => match classify(&e) {
   438              FrontendClass::Declined(what) => {
   439                  eprintln!("con-ron: declined: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   440                  return 2;
   441              }
   442              // A stream whose inductive block contradicts its own declarations
   443              // in a REDUNDANT field is rejected at the parse.
   444              FrontendClass::Invalid(what) => {
   445                  eprintln!("con-ron: invalid: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   446                  return 1;
   447              }
   448              FrontendClass::Internal(msg) => {
   449                  eprintln!("con-ron: {}:{}: {}", file, line, msg);
   450                  return 3;
   451              }
   452          },
   453          Ok((Ok(r), _)) => r,
   454      };
   455      // the in-process modeller's receipt
   456      if !parsed.in_modelled.is_empty() {
   457          let names: Vec<String> = parsed
   458              .in_modelled
   459              .iter()
   460              .map(|n| driver::name_of(pers, &st.store, n))
   461              .collect();
   462          eprintln!(
   463              "con-ron: {} inductive blocks modelled in-process: {} ({} generated \
   464               records, checked by the fold as declarations and not counted as records \
   465               of the file)",
   466              parsed.in_modelled.len(),
   467              names.join(", "),
   468              parsed.gen_records
   469          );
   470      }
   471      // the census (`CON_LECHE_INMODEL_CENSUS=1`): every mutual/nested block's
   472      // outcome, then stop — the parse only, no fold.  Exit 2, never 0.
   473      if census {
   474          for (n, why) in parsed.in_model_declined.iter() {
   475              eprintln!(
   476                  "con-ron: inmodel declined {}: {}",
   477                  driver::name_of(pers, &st.store, n),
   478                  con_ron::render::from_cps(why)
   479              );
   480          }
   481          eprintln!(
   482              "con-ron: inmodel census: {} modelled, {} declined ({}, parse only)",
   483              parsed.in_modelled.len(),
   484              parsed.in_model_declined.len(),
   485              mode_tag
   486          );
   487          return 2;
   488      }
   489      // the projection-function rewrite's receipt
   490      if !parsed.proj_rewrites.is_empty() {
   491          eprintln!(
   492              "con-ron: {} projection functions of non-direct structure-likes \
   493               rewritten to recursor form",
   494              parsed.proj_rewrites.len()
   495          );
   496          if std::env::var("CON_LECHE_PROJREC_TRACE").is_ok() {
   497              for n in parsed.proj_rewrites.iter() {
   498                  eprintln!("con-ron:   rewritten {}", driver::name_of(pers, &st.store, n));
   499              }
   500          }
   501      }
   502      let file_records = parsed.decls.len();
   503      let gen_records = parsed.gen_records;
   504      // From here on the store is the checker's state: the memo tables and the
   505      // per-declaration caches join it (`AState`), and every handle the parse
   506      // produced indexes into it.
   507      // **PREPARE** (`frontend::prepare`): what the fold runs over is
   508      // `prepare_prelude` of the file's records — the prelude's declarations
   509      // first (the stream's own copies where it has them, the rest synthesised),
   510      // then the stream's, with every pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
   511      // ground hoisted ahead of it.  It takes the whole state since task
   512      // #97-P4d: step 2 is the real ground hoist, which interns.
   513      let prepared = match prepare::prepare_d(pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed.decls) {
   514          Ok(p) => p,
   515          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   516      };
   517      // the ground hoist's receipt
   518      if !prepared.hoisted.is_empty() {
   519          let names: Vec<String> = prepared
   520              .hoisted
   521              .iter()
   522              .map(|n| driver::name_of(pers, &st.store, n))
   523              .collect();
   524          eprintln!(
   525              "con-ron: {} declarations hoisted ahead of the pinned Nat operations \
   526               they ground: {}",
   527              prepared.hoisted.len(),
   528              names.join(", ")
   529          );
   530      }
   531      let pins = match con_ron::driver::pins_for_run(&a.pins, a.no_pins) {
   532          Ok(p) => p,
   533          Err(e) => {
   534              eprintln!("con-ron: {}", e);
   535              return 3;
   536          }
   537      };
   538      // The heartbeat's first line: the parse and the preparation are done.
   539      let mut hb = Heartbeat::new(a.progress, t0);
   540      hb.parse_done(
   541          prepared.decls.len(),
   542          file_records,
   543          gen_records,
   544          prepared.synthesised,
   545          (
   546              st.store.node_count(pers),
   547              st.store.ls().node_count(pers),
   548              st.store.ns().node_count(pers),
   549          ),
   550      );
   551      // **THE STARTUP PIN WALK** (DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d, task #97-P4d): every
   552      // pinned datum the checker compares a stream record against — the six
   553      // basis blocks in both forms, the axiom pins, the reserved names and the
   554      // `Nat`-operation variants — interned ONCE, here, while the scratch tier
   555      // is still off, so that nothing the fold compares against lives in a tier
   556      // that is about to vanish.  Its result is the fold's pin parameter.
   557      let ipins = match checker::intern_all_pins(pers, &mut st, &pins) {
   558          Ok(p) => p,
   559          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   560      };
   561      // ONE driver, and the heartbeat is printed between its steps
   562      // (`driver::check_decls_driver`, which is `checker::check_decls_phased`
   563      // with the pool for its phase B).
   564      let jobs: u64 = match a.jobs {
   565          Some(n) => n,
   566          None => con_ron::driver::default_jobs(),
   567      };
   568      // ONE lane, whatever the flags: the driver is what freezes the persistent
   569      // tier at the phase boundary and phase B is the pool at every worker count
   570      // (task #97-P6-6b), so a run with no heartbeat is the same computation as
   571      // a run with one and `install_then_check` is no longer a second path.
   572      let verdict = if a.progress > 0 {
   573          driver::check_decls_driver(pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, &prepared.decls, jobs, &mut hb)
   574      } else {
   575          let mut silent = driver::Silent;
   576          driver::check_decls_driver(pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, &prepared.decls, jobs, &mut silent)
   577      };
   578      // **The headline number is the FILE's declaration-record count**: the
   579      // records the PARSE produced, which are the file's own, less the records
   580      // the in-process modeller generated.  Nothing the preparation does moves

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/pins.rs#L1-L60
     1  //! `arena::pins` — the reserved names, interned ONCE (task #97-P6-4a).
     2  //!
     3  //! con-leche compares its reserved names — `natName`, `natZeroName`,
     4  //! `natSuccName`, the sixteen `Nat`-operation names, the `Bool` trio, the
     5  //! `String`/`List`/`Char` family, the standard and the trusted axiom names —
     6  //! as `Name` VALUES, which Lean builds once per nullary `def` and caches.
     7  //! The arena compares them as HANDLES, so `arena::core::pin` turned each one
     8  //! into `intern_name` of a freshly built `Name`: a `code_points` allocation
     9  //! and an `Arc<NameNode>` per path segment, then one cons-table probe per
    10  //! segment, every time.  Task #97-P6-1's counter measured what that costs on
    11  //! `Init`: **140 083 646 `NStore::intern` calls, of which 88 854 033 are
    12  //! probes of a `str` node built purely to be compared and dropped** — tens of
    13  //! millions of rebuilds of about forty constants, in `natLitSupported`'s
    14  //! three probes per literal, in `natOpNames`, in `strLitToConstructor`.
    15  //!
    16  //! This module is DESIGN.md's answer, flagged at task #97c ("the `Pins`
    17  //! record that is NOT here") and deferred there for want of a number: one
    18  //! record, filled once at the driver by `intern_reserved_pins`, and every
    19  //! `pin` of a constant name becomes a field read.
    20  //!
    21  //! **Not `arena::checker`'s `intern_all_pins`.**  That one walks the `--pins`
    22  //! RECEIPT file (the trusted pin list) into the persistent tier; this one
    23  //! interns the checker's own reserved constants.  The two run at the same
    24  //! point of the pipeline and mean different things, which is why they have
    25  //! different names.
    26  //!
    27  //! ## The table is a `Vec`, and that is what kills task #97c's hazard
    28  //!
    29  //! Task #97c declined the record because of an initialisation-order hazard:
    30  //! "a pin read before it is filled compares against the zero word and
    31  //! silently says *not `Nat`*".  A record of handle FIELDS has that hazard,
    32  //! because every 32-bit word is a syntactically valid handle.  A `Vec<NIdx>`
    33  //! does not: before `intern_reserved_pins` runs the table is EMPTY, so `pin_at`
    34  //! takes its bounds branch and raises `CheckError::Internal` — a loud stop,
    35  //! never a quiet wrong answer.  The cost is one `len` compare per read,
    36  //! against an interning walk it replaces.
    37  //!
    38  //! ## What is pinned
    39  //!
    40  //! The forty-nine names below and `basis_names::reserved_basis_names()`'s
    41  //! nineteen, plus the three interned values every `pin` site around them
    42  //! needs: the empty universe-argument list, the level `0` and the expression
    43  //! `Sort 1` (`arena::core`'s `empty_levels`, `zero_level` and `sort_one`,
    44  //! which now read this record instead of interning).
    45  //!
    46  //! All of them go into the PERSISTENT tier, because `intern_reserved_pins` runs
    47  //! before the parse, while the scratch tier is closed.  That matters twice:
    48  //! a pinned handle must survive every `drop_scratch` (it is read across all
    49  //! of them), and task #97-P6-1's `pers_find_maybe` rests on "a persistent
    50  //! node's children are persistent", which the bottom-up intern of a closed
    51  //! scratch tier gives for free.
    52  //!
    53  //! **Denotation unchanged.**  A pin is `intern_name` of the same `Name`, so
    54  //! the handle this record holds is the handle `pin` computed before —
    55  //! `denoteN` is injective and `intern` is idempotent, so pre-interning a name
    56  //! the export also carries hands the export's parse the very same handle.
    57  //! What changes is only WHEN the intern happens, and how many times.
    58  //!
    59  //! Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:119-136 AState` (DESIGN.md §8.6's
    60  //! twin ledger, task #97-P6-4a) — `AState` gains a `pins : Pins` field and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/frontend/prepare.rs#L1-L50
     1  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/Prepare.lean` — **what happens between the
     2  //! file and the fold** (task #97 P4e part 1).
     3  //!
     4  //! `prepare_prelude` is total — no record of the stream is dropped, rewritten
     5  //! or retagged — and it does two things:
     6  //!
     7  //! 1. **the prelude's declarations first**, the stream's OWN copy of each
     8  //!    where the stream has one and a synthesised one only where it has none,
     9  //!    so a stream that declares the toolchain's `Bool` is checked on its own
    10  //!    `Bool` record;
    11  //! 2. **the ground hoist**: a pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
    12  //!    structural ground is moved ahead of it when the stream declares it
    13  //!    later.
    14  //!
    15  //! Moving a record earlier can only reject, never accept, which is why the
    16  //! spec con-leche proves is as simple as it is:
    17  //!
    18  //! ```text
    19  //! ∃ extra, (∀ d ∈ extra, d ∈ prelude) ∧
    20  //!   (preparePrelude ds).toList.Perm (ds.toList ++ extra)
    21  //! ```
    22  //!
    23  //! **Step 2 is `frontend::nat_op_ground`'s**, a module of its own exactly as
    24  //! con-leche's is (task #97-P4d; task #97-P4e part 1 shipped an identity
    25  //! placeholder here, because the pass needs the kernel's
    26  //! `natOpNames`/`natDivModNames`, which arrived with the pins).  It is why
    27  //! `prepare_d` takes the whole `AState` where everything else in this module
    28  //! needs only the store.
    29  //!
    30  //! **Where the store comes from.**  Only `prelude_key`, whose `.anonymous`
    31  //! fall-through has to be INTERNED, and the two functions that call it;
    32  //! [`pick_idx`] and [`declares`] are pure, exactly as con-leche's are, because
    33  //! `env::i_declaration_names` is (`arena/env.rs`'s `table_name` note).
    34  //! Nothing in this module reads or writes a term.
    35  //!
    36  //! **The deviation of the port into the verified core** (task #84), kept
    37  //! verbatim from `con_ron_core::frontend::prepare`: con-leche's `pick` ERASES
    38  //! the picked record from the array (`Array.eraseIdxIfInBounds`) and `frontOf`
    39  //! moves it to the front.  The Aeneas subset has no operation that takes an
    40  //! element out of a `Vec` — no `remove`, no `pop`, no `into_iter` — so the
    41  //! port splits the two halves that con-leche fuses: [`pick_idx`] is the cited
    42  //! `ds.findIdx (declares n)` with the erasure recorded in a `picked` mask
    43  //! instead of performed, [`front_of`] runs that over the prelude, and
    44  //! [`prepared_stream`] materialises the whole prepared list in ONE pass.  The
    45  //! list that comes out is the same list; the cost is one record copy per
    46  //! record, where the copied fields are handles and `Vec` spines and not terms.
    47  //! con-leche's `pickSpec`/`frontSpec` are not ported (they are `cons`-list
    48  //! specifications with no caller on the run path); `pick_spec` lives in this
    49  //! module's tests, where it still checks `pick_idx` against the specification
    50  //! on every `cargo test`.

  1613                  Ok(()) => intern_pin_sets(pers, st, pins, 0, Vec::new()),
  1614              },
  1615          },
  1616      }
  1617  }

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L885-L930
   885  // `IO.FS.Handle.read` has no model, and a theorem about the file is a
   886  // theorem about its bytes.
   887  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   888  
   889  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/ExportC.lean:903-931 parseExportHandleD
   890  /// **The file handle as the parse's `ChunkSource`**: each `next_chunk` is one
   891  /// `read_up_to` of `chunk` bytes, strictly forward, handed over whole; the
   892  /// first empty read is the end of the input.  A failed read ends the input
   893  /// the same way and is KEPT here, and `parse_export_handle_d` reports it in
   894  /// place of whatever the parse of the truncated input said — so a read error
   895  /// is exit 3, never a verdict, as before the loop moved.
   896  pub struct HandleSource<'a, R: Read> {
   897      /// The open reader.
   898      pub h: &'a mut R,
   899      /// The buffer size, `export_c::CHUNK_SIZE` in the binary.
   900      pub chunk: usize,
   901      /// The nonempty buffers handed out so far, for the heartbeat.
   902      pub chunks: u64,
   903      /// The first read failure, if any.
   904      pub err: Option<std::io::Error>,
   905  }
   906  
   907  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/ExportC.lean:903-931 parseExportHandleD
   908  impl<'a, R: Read> ChunkSource for HandleSource<'a, R> {
   909      /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/ExportC.lean:903-931 parseExportHandleD
   910      /// One read of up to `chunk` bytes; empty at the end or on a failure.
   911      fn next_chunk(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
   912          if self.err.is_some() {
   913              return Vec::new();
   914          }
   915          let mut buf: Vec<u8> = vec![0u8; self.chunk];
   916          match read_up_to(self.h, &mut buf) {
   917              Ok(n) => {
   918                  buf.truncate(n);
   919                  if n > 0 {
   920                      self.chunks += 1;
   921                  }
   922                  buf
   923              }
   924              Err(e) => {
   925                  self.err = Some(e);
   926                  Vec::new()
   927              }
   928          }
   929      }
   930  }

   244  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/Types.lean:155-169 Modeller` —
   245  /// **the modeller seam** (DESIGN.md §8.2's `Modeller`).  One method: a block
   246  /// in, the model records it generates in stream order or the reason it is
   247  /// declined.  Handles in, handles out — nothing in (B) may build an `Expr`
   248  /// tree, and a default instantiation that called con-leche's own generator on
   249  /// read-back terms would do exactly that.
   250  ///
   251  /// **Why a trait and not a function pointer** (`in_model_rec`'s reason,
   252  /// unchanged): a trait method on a type parameter extracts as a *typeclass
   253  /// field* — an opaque function of the quantified `Self` — so the extracted
   254  /// parse is quantified over an arbitrary modeller and a later refinement
   255  /// carries one hypothesis about its output rather than a port of four
   256  /// thousand lines whose correctness decides coverage and not soundness.  A
   257  /// `dyn` object or a function pointer is outside the subset (DESIGN.md §3.4).
   258  ///
   259  /// The store is in hand because the twin's method is in `AM`: a generated
   260  /// record's terms are handles, and building one means interning it.
   261  pub trait Modeller {
   262      /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/InModel.lean:39-45 generate

   265          &self,
   266      pers: &PersTier,
   267          ar: &mut EStore,
   268          ctx: &ModelCtx,
   269          b: &BlockRec,
   270      ) -> Result<Vec<IDeclaration>, Vec<u32>>;
   271  }

== crates/con-ron/src/in_model.rs#L1-L30
     1  //! `ConLeche/Frontend/InModel.lean` — **the modeller seam, instantiated by
     2  //! delegation** (DESIGN.md §8.2, task #97 P4f), the Rust side of the Lean
     3  //! twin's `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/InModel.lean`.
     4  //!
     5  //! `con_ron_core::frontend::types::Modeller` is the arena's one-method seam:
     6  //! handles in, handles out.  What fills it here is **`crates/con-ron`'s own
     7  //! in-process modeller, unchanged** — the 6 200 lines of
     8  //! `crate::in_model::{kit, mutual, nested}` that the shipping binary runs —
     9  //! with a readback in front of it and an intern behind it:
    10  //!
    11  //! ```text
    12  //! BlockRec over handles  --denote-->  con-ron-core's BlockRec (Expr trees)
    13  //!                                       |  crate::in_model::generate
    14  //!                                       v
    15  //! Vec<IDeclaration>      <--intern--  Vec<Declaration>
    16  //! ```
    17  //!
    18  //! **This is the twin's own instantiation, one representation down.**  The
    19  //! Lean reads the block back, calls *con-leche's* generator and interns what
    20  //! comes out; the Rust reads the block back, calls *con-ron's port of that
    21  //! generator* and interns what comes out.  So the two binaries of the
    22  //! differential sweep run the SAME unverified modeller: `con-ron` calls it on
    23  //! the trees its parser builds, `con-ron` calls it on the trees this
    24  //! module reads back out of the store.  A block modelled differently by the
    25  //! two would be a difference the sweep could not attribute, and there is now
    26  //! no way for one to arise.
    27  //!
    28  //! **Nothing here is verified and nothing here needs to be** (DESIGN.md §8.2,
    29  //! and con-leche's own module note): a wrong generated record is rejected or
    30  //! declined by the fold, never accepted, so this layer decides *coverage* and

     2  //!
     3  //! The Rust twin of `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean`, which is con-leche's
     4  //! `Kernel/Checker.lean`'s `checkDecl`/`checkDeclsPure` and
     5  //! `Cached/Installed.lean`'s two-phase `checkDecls`.
     6  //!
     7  //! ## Two folds, and which is which
     8  //!
     9  //! * **`check_decls_pure`** is the THEOREM's shape —
    10  //!   `ConLeche/Model/Fold.lean`'s `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` consumes it, and
    11  //!   DESIGN.md §8.2's Theorem 1 folds `checkDecl` over the stream.  One step
    12  //!   per record, install and check together.
    13  //! * **`install_then_check`** is what the BINARY runs: phase A installs every
    14  //!   record, annotating its header and its value but not inferring; phase B
    15  //!   checks each recorded declaration against the PREFIX VIEW it was installed
    16  //!   at.  con-leche proves the two are the same accept
    17  //!   (`fullyChecked_checkDecls`); the arena's two call the same `checkDecl`
    18  //!   pieces, which is what keeps them the same computation.
    19  //!
    20  //! ## Every step is bracketed
    21  //!
    22  //! DESIGN.md §8.3: "Persistent = parse + installed environment; scratch = one
    23  //! declaration's check."  Both phases and both folds run each record inside
    24  //! `enter_scratch` … `drop_scratch`.  Phase B's `check_pending` brackets
    25  //! `check_value_group`, and every node it appends goes with the tier.  Phase
    26  //! A's `annot_step` brackets the install too (the fallback `annot_step_other`
    27  //! included), because annotation infers and inference interns: `promote`
    28  //! copies exactly what leaves the step — the installed constants and the
    29  //! pending record — to the persistent tier before the drop (see `annot_step`).
    30  //! `check_decls_pure`'s step, `check_decl_step`, is bracketed the same way.
    31  //!
    32  //! ## The pins are interned at startup
    33  //!
    34  //! `intern_all_pins` is DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d's one-time tree walk, and it is what
    35  //! makes every later `pin`/`intern_ci` of the same datum return the PERSISTENT
    36  //! handle whatever tier is live (§8.3: `intern` probes the persistent table
    37  //! first).  Without it a reserved name first interned inside a scratch tier
    38  //! would compare unequal to the stream's own persistent copy of it, which is
    39  //! the one way hash-consing can go wrong across the tier boundary.
    40  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L927-L961
   927  pub fn annot_step(
   928      pers: &PersTier,
   929      st: &mut AState,
   930      mode: &CheckMode,
   931      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   932      i: u64,
   933      fe: IFEnv,
   934      pend: Vec<PendingCheck>,
   935      pd: &IDeclaration,
   936  ) -> Result<(IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>), CheckError> {
   937      let vis: u64 = fe.visible_below;
   938      flush_caches(st);
   939      enter_scratch(st);
   940      match annot_step_go(pers, st, mode, pins, fe, pd) {
   941          Err(e) => Err(e),
   942          Ok((fe2, vg_opt)) => {
   943              let k: u64 = fe2.visible_below - vis;
   944              match vg_opt {
   945                  None => match promote_new(pers, st, PMemo::empty(), CORE_WALK_FUEL, k, fe2) {
   946                      Err(e) => Err(e),
   947                      Ok((_, fe3)) => {
   948                          drop_scratch(st);
   949                          Ok((fe3, pend))
   950                      }
   951                  },
   952                  Some(vg) => annot_step_promote(pers, st, i, vis, k, fe2, pend, vg),
   953              }
   954          }
   955      }
   956  }
   957

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L470-L565
   470  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean:438-455 checkDecls
   471  /// con-leche: Main.lean:318-421 checkDeclsIO
   472  /// **The driver**: `checker::check_decls_phased` with the boundary visible —
   473  /// a straight line of calls into the verified crate, with the observer's
   474  /// lines between them and the pool in the place of phase B's sequential walk
   475  /// (task #97-P5-Driver):
   476  ///
   477  /// | step | here | in `check_decls_phased` |
   478  /// |---|---|---|
   479  /// | phase A | `checker::annot_fold_hooked(…, fold_start(), ds, 0, obs)` | the same call |
   480  /// | boundary | `checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store)` | the same call |
   481  /// | phase B | `pool::check_pool(&tier, mode, &fe, &pend, &st.pins, workers, …)` | `checker::check_pending_worker(&tier, mode, &fe, &st.pins, &pend)` |
   482  /// | after | `checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier)` | the same call |
   483  ///
   484  /// Everything else here is the observer, which only ever holds `&` the state
   485  /// (the hook of phase A by the trait's own signature, the other lines through
   486  /// `&st.store`), so it cannot change an outcome.  So the capstone, whose
   487  /// stage 6 is `PoolAccepts` (phase A, the freeze, and one accepting
   488  /// `checker::check_pending_worker` per worker over the records it checked,
   489  /// together covering the pending list; task #97-P5-POOL), is about this
   490  /// function modulo the pool's one claim: that its accept has that shape
   491  /// (`pool.rs`'s note states it and what it rests on).
   492  ///
   493  /// **The boundary is where the tier is FROZEN** (task #97-P6-6b).  Phase A
   494  /// owns its persistent tier and appends to it; at the boundary
   495  /// `checker::freeze_tier` moves the four stores' persistent tables out into
   496  /// one `PersTier` and sets the `shared_on` flags that make every later
   497  /// persistent read go to it and every persistent append a decline.  The
   498  /// installed index goes to the workers by reference, since `check_pending`
   499  /// takes the visibility bound as a scalar — so `n` workers share one
   500  /// environment and one term DAG and own nothing but a scratch tier, their
   501  /// caches and a copy of the pin handles (`checker::worker_state`).
   502  pub fn check_decls_driver<O: PhaseObserver + InstallHook + Send>(
   503      pers: &PersTier,
   504      st: &mut AState,
   505      mode: &CheckMode,
   506      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   507      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   508      jobs: u64,
   509      obs: &mut O,
   510  ) -> Result<IFEnv, (CheckError, u64)> {
   511      let total = ds.len();
   512      // PHASE A: the verified fold, the heartbeat's install line as its hook.
   513      let p = match checker::annot_fold_hooked(pers, st, mode, pins, checker::fold_start(), ds, 0, &*obs) {
   514          Err(e) => {
   515              obs.install_failed(e.1, total);
   516              return Err(e);
   517          }
   518          Ok(p) => p,
   519      };
   520      let (n_installed, fe, pend): (u64, IFEnv, Vec<PendingCheck>) = p;
   521      let m = pend.len();
   522      obs.install_done(pers, &st.store, total, m);
   523      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   524      obs.phase_b_workers(workers);
   525      // THE PHASE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier leaves the state and becomes a
   526      // value every worker reads (the doc comment above).  `st` keeps its
   527      // (empty) store with the flags set, so the observer can still read a
   528      // label back through the shared tier.
   529      let tier: PersTier = match checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store) {
   530          Err(e) => {
   531              obs.check_failed(n_installed);
   532              return Err((e, n_installed));
   533          }
   534          Ok(t) => t,
   535      };
   536      // PHASE B, `checker::check_pending_worker`'s walk on `workers` threads:
   537      // every record checked by `checker::check_pending` at its own prefix
   538      // view, inside its own scratch tier, on its worker's state
   539      // (`checker::worker_state`), the results merged by record index and
   540      // walked in record order — so the verdict and the record a rejection
   541      // names are the one-worker walk's at every `--jobs`.
   542      let lock = std::sync::Mutex::new(obs);
   543      let r = crate::pool::check_pool(&tier, mode, &fe, &pend, &st.pins, workers, &lock);
   544      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   545          Ok(o) => o,
   546          Err(e) => e.into_inner(),
   547      };
   548      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the fold — the verdict line's
   549      // declaration label, the failing record's name, the receipts — reads a
   550      // handle back out of `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has
   551      // gone out of scope answers `None` to every one of them (the first
   552      // version of this printed `at theorem ?` where the tip printed `at
   553      // theorem addOk`).  `thaw_tier` is `freeze_tier` inverted.
   554      checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   555      match r {
   556          Err((e, pos)) => {
   557              obs.check_failed(pos);
   558              Err((e, pos))
   559          }
   560          Ok(()) => {
   561              obs.check_done(m);
   562              Ok(fe)
   563          }
   564      }
   565  }

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L17-L41
    17  //!
    18  //! ## What a worker is
    19  //!
    20  //! §8.3 has said since P1 what phase B is: "the persistent tier is immutable
    21  //! in phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — **no atomics anywhere**",
    22  //! and task #97-P6-6 verified it in the code (`check_pending` is the bracket;
    23  //! `intern_persistent`'s only caller is phase A's `arena::promote`).  So a
    24  //! worker is
    25  //!
    26  //!   * its own `AState`, `checker::worker_state(pins)` — an EMPTY store whose
    27  //!     four `shared_on` flags are set, its own `Memos`, its own `Caches`, and
    28  //!     a COPY of the driver's `Pins` (sixty-eight handles into the persistent
    29  //!     tier, so a copy is two `Vec<NIdx>` and three words);
    30  //!   * `&PersTier`, the persistent tier the driver froze at the phase
    31  //!     boundary (`checker::freeze_tier`) and every worker reads;
    32  //!   * `&IFEnv`, the installed index — **by reference, and this is what task
    33  //!     #97-P6-6b's second half bought**.  `check_pending` used to take the
    34  //!     index BY VALUE so that it could restrict it to the record's prefix
    35  //!     bound; a worker would have needed `ifenv_dup`, which DESIGN.md (task
    36  //!     #97-P6-6b) prices at ≈1.4 GB a worker on Mathlib.  The bound is a scalar
    37  //!     parameter now (`pc.vis`), so the environment is shared and **a worker
    38  //!     costs no environment copy at all**.
    39  //!
    40  //! Every sequential piece of that — the freeze, the worker's state, the
    41  //! per-record check — is the VERIFIED crate's since task #97-P5-Driver, and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L1474-L1491
  1474  /// con-leche: Main.lean:262-278 checkWorker
  1475  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Phased.lean:37-44 AState.worker` — the twin's
  1476  /// phase-B worker reads the persistent tier where it is.
  1477  /// **A phase-B worker's start state** (task #97-P6-6b's `pool::worker_state`,
  1478  /// moved here by task #97-P5-Driver): an empty store whose four `shared_on`
  1479  /// flags are up, so that every persistent read goes to the `PersTier` the
  1480  /// boundary froze and a persistent append is declined; fresh memos and caches;
  1481  /// and a copy of the pins.  The scratch tier is off until `check_pending`
  1482  /// opens it.
  1483  pub fn worker_state(pins: &Pins) -> AState {
  1484      let mut st = AState::init(EStore::empty());
  1485      st.store.shared_on = true;
  1486      st.store.lss.shared_on = true;
  1487      st.store.lss.ls.shared_on = true;
  1488      st.store.lss.ls.ns.shared_on = true;
  1489      st.pins = pins_dup(pins);
  1490      st
  1491  }

   151  /// con-leche: Main.lean:48-51 ConLeche.CheckError.exitCode
   152  /// The cited three codes, plus the port's own fourth constructor
   153  /// (`core_types::CheckError::Native`, DESIGN.md §3's ruling of 2026-09-13):
   154  /// a failure with no con-leche counterpart — a machine-word limit, a width
   155  /// check — is a **decline**, exit 2, the same code as "not implemented",
   156  /// because that is what it is: the port cannot carry this input, and says so
   157  /// rather than rejecting the stream (1) or claiming a checker bug (3).
   158  pub fn exit_code(e: &CheckError) -> u8 {
   159      match e {
   160          CheckError::NotImplemented(_) => 2,
   161          CheckError::Invalid(_) => 1,
   162          CheckError::Internal(_) => 3,
   163          CheckError::Native(_) => 2,
   164      }

== proof/ConRon/Arena/Denote.lean#L181-L206
   181  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:344-354 Expr — the fuel-indexed
   182  readback of an expression handle. -/
   183  def denoteEAux (st : EStore) : Nat → EIdx → Option Expr
   184    | 0, _ => none
   185    | f + 1, i =>
   186      (st.view i).bind fun v =>
   187        match v with
   188        | .bvar k => some (.bvar k)
   189        | .fvar k ty => (denoteEAux st f ty).map (Expr.fvar k)
   190        | .sort u => (denoteL st.ls u).map Expr.sort
   191        | .const n us => opt2 Expr.const (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteLs st.lss us)
   192        | .app g a => opt2 Expr.app (denoteEAux st f g) (denoteEAux st f a)
   193        | .lam ty b m =>
   194          opt2 (fun x y => Expr.lam x y m) (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   195        | .forallE ty b m =>
   196          opt2 (fun x y => Expr.forallE x y m) (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   197        | .letE ty w b =>
   198          opt3 Expr.letE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f w) (denoteEAux st f b)
   199        | .lit l => some (.lit l)
   200        | .proj n k e =>
   201          opt2 (fun nm x => Expr.proj nm k x) (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteEAux st f e)
   202  
   203  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:344-354 Expr — the readback of an
   204  expression handle, at the store's own node count as fuel. -/
   205  def denoteE (st : EStore) (i : EIdx) : Option Expr :=
   206    denoteEAux st (st.nodeCount + 1) i

== proof/ConRon/Arena/WF.lean#L1-L40
     1  /-
     2  # Store well-formedness and the store layer's theorems (DESIGN.md §8.3, P2a)
     3  
     4  `StoreWF` is the arena's own invariant — con-leche's `TWF`
     5  (`Setlec/Kernel/ArenaWF.lean:900`, 28 clauses) redrawn for the
     6  per-constructor, high-tag representation.  It lives here, beside the
     7  implementation, importing nothing from `ConRon.Refine`: con-leche's lesson 27,
     8  "implementation may import a *self-contained* data-structure verification".
     9  
    10  Each store's invariant is `∃ rank, …WFAt st rank`.  The rank is existential
    11  because nothing at runtime stores it (DESIGN §8.3: "zero runtime cost, and no
    12  global array order is needed with per-constructor arrays"); what it buys is
    13  
    14  * **acyclicity**, hence a terminating `denote`;
    15  * **a fuel bound**: a persistent node's rank is below the persistent node
    16    count and a scratch node's below the total, so `nodeCount + 1` — the fuel
    17    `denoteE` uses — is always enough, and `dropScratch` shrinks both sides of
    18    the persistent clause together.
    19  
    20  The clauses, in the order a reader meets them:
    21  
    22  | clause | what it says |
    23  |---|---|
    24  | `childOK` | every child is in range, ranked below its parent, and persistent if the parent is |
    25  | `rankP` / `rankS` | ranks are below the tier's node count (the fuel bound) |
    26  | `consP` / `consS` | each tier's cons table is exactly the inverse of that tier's `get` |
    27  | `fresh` | a scratch cons entry never duplicates a persistent one (DESIGN §8.3's cross-tier canonicity; con-leche's `t_cons_fresh`) |
    28  | `derExact` | the derived column is `derOfView` of the node — *locally*; the global `derived st i = e.data` is a theorem (`derived_exact`) |
    29  | `sized` | the derived array is as long as the node array |
    30  | `cap` | no constructor array exceeds 2^27 entries, so a handle's 27-bit index is injective on it |
    31  | `bmKey` | every binder key a cons table holds names a datum the store can decode |
    32  | `scrOff` | the scratch tier is empty while the scratch flag is off |
    33  | `sync` | the nesting's scratch flags move together (task #97a) |
    34  
    35  `childOK`'s third conjunct — *persistent parents have persistent children* —
    36  is what makes `dropScratch` sound: without it a persistent node could point
    37  into a tier that is about to vanish.  It needs no hypothesis at `intern`,
    38  because `scrOff` makes a scratch handle undecodable while the flag is off, so
    39  a valid child of a node appended to the persistent tier is persistent already.
    40  -/
